prompt: Write an essay about committing to a career at a young age.
text:
Should kids have to pick what they want to do for their whole life when they are like 14? i dont think so. My cousin knew he wanted to be a surgeon since he was in 5th grade and now hes in med school and he seems happy but he also never really tried anything else. My mom says thats good because you dont waste time but i think it kinda sucks to be locked in before you even know what the world is like.

The other side is that if you start early you get more time to get good at something. Like if you know you want to be a musician you can practice every day and by the time your 20 you already have experience. My friend Ana started coding at 12 and now she has a internship at a company and everybody says shes way ahead.

But not everybody changes their mind like that. Lots of people at my school say they want to be a doctor or lawyer just because their parents said so. I think the real problem is that schools make you choose too early. In my opinion you should be allowed to try stuff and change your mind without feeling like youre failing. So yeah commitment is good but only if its your own choice and not something you got pushed into when you were too young to know better.

prompt: Write an essay about committing to a career at a young age.
text:
Nowadays many young people must decide their career when they are very young. In my opinion this is both good and bad. On one hand, when a child decides early, he can start learning and practicing his skill in the right time. For example, in my country some families send their children to study music at the age of ten, and they become very professional when they grow up. This commitment give them a big advantage.

On the other hand, the young age is not the age of wisdom. A fourteen years old student does not know yet what he likes or what the job market will be in twenty years. Many of my friends choose engineering because their father is engineer, not because they love it. After some years they feel stuck and they cannot change easily, because they already spent money and time on their studies.

In the other hand, I think the best solution is the balance. Students should be exposed to many fields in school, and they should be encouraged to explore. When they are older, maybe sixteen or seventeen, they can commit to a career with more understanding. So, the commitment is important, but it must come from the inside of the person and not from the pressure of the family or society.

prompt: Write an essay about committing to a career at a young age.
text:
Today the question of career commitment at young age is very actual. Some people think that children should choose profession early, for example at the age of fourteen or fifteen. They say that if you know what you want, you have more time to become expert. I agree with this partly, because in the life it is important to have goal.

However, the early choice has also problems. Young person cannot understand yet what is the real work, and often he chooses the profession because of the fashion or because of the parents. For example, my classmate wanted to be the pilot, but when he started studying physics he understood that he hates the mathematics. Now he is studying the economics and he is not happy. If he had more time, he would not waste the years.

From the other side, the society needs the people who know what they do. The early commitment can give the motivation for study. The children who are doing the sport from the childhood often become the champions, and the same is true for the music or the programming.

In my opinion, the best way is to give the teenagers the choice but not force them. The school should show them the different professions, and the parents should listen. So the commitment will be the result of the thinking, not the decision made in the hurry.

prompt: Write an essay about committing to a career at a young age.
text:
Choosing a career at a young age is something a lot of students have to deal with way before they're ready. Supporters say early commitment lets you build skills steadily and get real expertise over time. Like, a teen who knows they wanna be a doctor can take hard science classes and volunteer, which helps a ton later.

Critics say teens don't really know themselves yet. Interests change, job markets shift, and a choice made at 14 can feel like a cage by 25. Plus if your family is pushing you, you might end up in a field that doesn't fit your talents or values.

I think the sensible answer is somewhere in the middle. Schools should expose kids to lots of fields and let them explore without getting punished for switching. Commitment should look more like a bunch of provisional choices that get deeper over time, not one big irreversible verdict.

The goal isn't to put off decisions forever though. It's to make them with real understanding. Early commitment can be great when it comes from genuine curiosity, but when it's forced it becomes a burden. Young people deserve a chance to figure out who they are before the world tells them what to be.

text:

Real busy is different. Like during finals week when i had practice and homework and my little sister needed help with her science project. Thats hard and i didnt sleep well. But i got through it and i was proud. So maybe busy is only good when you chose it and you know why.

In my opinion we should stop equating busy with important. Being free to think or hang out with friends is not lazy. Anyway i need to go finish my history reading which i definitely didnt start yet.

prompt: Write an essay about being busy.
text:
Nowadays, almost everyone complains that they are very busy. People say they have no time for family, no time for friends, and no time for themselves. In my opinion, this feeling of being busy has become a kind of status in our society. When someone says he is busy, it looks like he is important and successful.

However, being busy is not always the same as being productive. Many people spend the day answering messages and attending meetings that do not add any value. They are busy but they are not achieving much. I have a cousin who works in a bank, and he tells me that he is always running, but at the end of the month he does not know what he really accomplished.

On the other hand, there are situations when being busy is necessary. Students preparing for the exams, doctors in the emergency room, and parents taking care of small children have really heavy schedules, and they cannot avoid it. The problem is not the activity itself but the lack of choice and balance.

To conclude, I believe we should learn to distinguish between useful busyness and empty busyness. We should prioritize what matters, and we should accept that we cannot do everything. Only then we can live a life that is calmer and more meaningful.

prompt: Write an essay about being busy.
text:
In the modern world, the people are always busy. Everyone has the job, the family, the studies, the social media and many other things. When I ask my friends how they are, the most common answer is: I am so busy. It seems that being busy became the norm and even the sign of the success.

I think this situation is not healthy. The busy person has no time for the rest, and the rest is very important for the brain and the body. Also, the busy life makes people less attentive to the relationships. For example, my uncle works in the company from morning till night, and he almost never sees his children. When he finally comes home, he is too tired to talk with them.

On the other side, it is not always the bad thing. Sometimes the busyness is the result of the big goals, and the people who work hard can achieve the success. The problem appears when the busyness is the escape from the real questions, for example, from the question what we really want.

In my opinion, every person should find the balance. It is necessary to make the list of priorities and to refuse the unnecessary tasks. Only in this way the time becomes the resource and not the enemy.

prompt: Write an essay about being busy.
text:
Being busy has kinda become a social currency. When people ask how were doing, the answer is usually some version of 'I have so much going on.' But busyness on its own says very little about whether a life is well spent. A packed calendar can reflect purpose, but it can also reflect bad boundaries, habit, or not being able to say no.

Part of the problem is busyness gets mistaken for productivity. Constant motion feels like progress even when the important stuff doesnt get done. Lots of people spend their days answering messages and sitting in meetings that add nothing, then wonder why their goals are still untouched.

Thats not to say intense periods arent unavoidable. A nurse on a long shift, a student before finals, a parent with little kids, they can be legitimately overwhelmed. The question is whether the demands are chosen, understood, and temporary, or if they've quietly become the permanent setup.

So the answer isnt to stop working hard. Its to be deliberate. Clear priorities, honest limits, and actual rest let you tell meaningful work from just motion. A full life and a crowded life arent the same thing.

The good part is obvious. Like my grandma can video call us from across the country, and kids in villages can learn stuff from youtube that their school doesnt have. Medicine got better too because doctors can look at scans really fast. Thats a big deal.

But there is a bad side too. Lots of my friends scroll on their phones till like 2 am and then they are tired in class. Some people cant even talk to each other face to face anymore without feeling weird. And honestly the amount of fake news is crazy, i saw something last week that was totally made up and i almost shared it.

So is technology good or bad? I think its neither, its like a tool. A hammer can build a house or hurt somebody. It depends on how we use it. Im not saying we should throw our phones away, but we should maybe put them down sometimes and look up.

prompt: Write an essay about the impact of technology.
text:
Technology has changed our life in many ways. In the past, people needed many days to send a letter to their families in other cities, but now we can send a message in one second. This is one of the greatest benefits of technology. Also, the students can search for any information in the internet, so the education became more easy and more available for everyone.

However, technology has also negative effects. Many people, especially young people, spend long hours in front of the screens. As a result, they have less time for physical activity and for family. Some of them even lost their ability to concentrate on reading a book for a long time. I think this is a serious problem for the future of our society.

Another problem is the privacy. Companies collect our information every day, and most people do not know how it is used. For this reason, I believe the governments should make strong laws to protect the citizens.

In conclusion, technology is a powerful tool that can bring many advantages, but we must use it wisely. We should be the masters of the technology, not its slaves.

prompt: Write an essay about the impact of technology.
text:
Technology has the great impact on the modern life. Nowadays, almost every person has the smartphone, and it is difficult to imagine the day without the internet. The technology helps us in the work, in the study and in the communication. For example, the doctors can consult the patients from the distance, and the students can take the online courses from the best universities of the world.

But the technology also has the negative side. The children spend the most of the time with the tablets and the phones, and they do not play outside as the children did in the past. The adults also suffer from the constant notifications, and the attention becomes very short. I have noticed that even myself I cannot read the long article without checking the messages.

Moreover, the question of the privacy is very serious. The companies know about us almost everything, from the places we visit to the things we buy. Many people do not think about it, but the information can be used in the bad way.

To sum up, the technology is not good or bad by itself. It depends on how the people use it. We need to learn the balance between the digital world and the real world, and I think it is the main challenge for our generation.

prompt: Write an essay about the impact of technology.
text:
Few things have changed everyday life as fast as technology. Communication that used to take weeks now takes seconds, and info that once needed a library trip fits in your pocket. For students, workers, and researchers, this has opened up access to knowledge in ways earlier generations couldn't have imagined.

But the same tools that connect us can also chop up our attention. All the notifications train us into bad habits, and a lot of people say they can't focus on a long text or a real conversation anymore. Privacy is another worry. Companies collect tons of data about our behavior, and most of us never really agreed to that.

These problems don't make technology evil. How it affects us depends a lot on how it's designed and how we use it. Smart regulation, better digital literacy classes, and some personal self-control can all help people get the good stuff without the costs.

Basically technology is a powerful tool, not something that acts on people on its own. The big challenge for the next few decades is making sure human judgment, not just convenience, shapes how these things get built and used.

My grandmother would have needed a full miracle for that. I cried a little, and nobody needed to know.

text:
Some people in my state want to make high school only three years instead of four. I think thats a interesting idea but i have mixed feelings about it. On one hand it would save families money and kids could start college or jobs earlier. My cousin is in a different country and their school is shorter and she says she felt ready to move on.

On the other hand, four years gives you time. Like i took a art class in 10th grade that i never would have tried if i had to rush. And junior year is when i figured out i liked chemistry, so if i had only three years i might never have found it. Also sports and clubs need time to really develop, and not everyone is ready for college at 17.

I think the real issue is not the number of years but what happens in them. If they cut a year but keep all the same classes, its just stress. But if they make it more focused, with more internships and real skills, it could work great. Honestly i think they should try a pilot program first and see. Thats what i would tell the school board if they asked me, which they wont.

prompt: Write an essay about a three-year high school program.
text:
The idea of reducing high school to three years has been discussed in our country recently. Supporters say that this program will save time and money for the families and the government. Also, students can enter the university earlier and start their career at a younger age. In my opinion, this advantage is important, especially for students who want to work and help their families.

However, I am not sure that three years are enough to prepare students for the university. In the last year of high school, students usually study the hardest subjects and they take the national exams. If we remove one year, the students will have less time to learn the basic knowledge, and the quality of education may decrease. Furthermore, the students need time to discover their talents and interests.

On the other hand, the government can make the program more efficient. For example, the schools can focus on the essential subjects and offer practical training, so the students become ready for the job market. This way, the shorter program can be a good choice.

To conclude, I believe the three-year program should be tested carefully before it is applied in all schools. The most important thing is not the length of the time but the quality of the learning.

prompt: Write an essay about a three-year high school program.
text:
Nowadays the discussion about the three-year high school is very popular in our country. Some officials say that the program will be more effective and the students will finish the school faster. They also say that the budget will save the money, because the education costs a lot for the state. I understand these arguments, but I have some doubts.

First of all, the three years is the short time for the complex material. In the fourth year the students usually repeat the main subjects and prepare for the exams. Without this year, many pupils will enter the university without the solid base in mathematics and the languages. I have seen it myself with my cousin, who entered the institute after the school and had the big problems with the physics.

On the other hand, the time is not always the key factor. If the program is well organized and the teachers have the good methods, the students can learn the same material in less time. The most important is the quality of the lessons, not the number of the years.

So, in my opinion, the three-year program can be useful, but only if the government invests in the teachers and the resources. Otherwise it will be the cheap reform which harms the future of the young people.

prompt: Write an essay about a three-year high school program.
text:
Proposals to shorten high school to three years have gotten attention in a few regions. It promises lower costs for families and earlier entry into work or university, which is appealing for students who are already doing well academically and can't really afford another year of tuition or lost wages.

But critics wonder if a squeezed curriculum can still have the same depth. The last year usually has advanced classes, exam prep, and time for students to figure out what they're into. If you cut it, a lot of grads might not be ready for hard university programs, especially in math and science.

Maybe a better approach is to redesign the curriculum instead of just deleting a year. Schools could focus on core skills, mix in hands-on learning, and set up real internships. That way you get efficiency without losing the breadth a full education needs.

The length of high school probably matters less than what kids actually learn in it. Any change should be piloted and evaluated first, so the decision is based on evidence and not just on budget stress.

text:
Self reliance means you can do stuff on your own without needing everybody to help you all the time. My grandpa is like the most self reliant guy ever. He fixes his own car and grows tomatoes and he never asks for help even when he should. My mom says he is stubborn but i think its kind of cool.

I think its important to learn basic stuff yourself. Like cooking, budgeting, how to change a tire, how to deal with a problem without panicking. When i moved into my dorm last year i had to figure out a lot of things and i felt proud when i got my laundry right the first time lol.

But self reliance can go too far. Some people refuse help even when they really need it and then they burn out or make mistakes that could have been avoided. Asking for help is not weak. Actually its smart because nobody knows everything. My friend Jordan wouldnt tell anyone he was struggling with his grades and he ended up failing a class.

So i think the goal is to be able to take care of yourself but also know when to call someone. Like being independent doesnt mean being alone. Thats what i learned anyway, even if i still forget sometimes.

prompt: Write an essay about self-reliance.
text:
Self-reliance means that a person depends on his own abilities and resources to solve problems and to achieve his goals. In my opinion, this is one of the most important qualities that a person can have. A self-reliant person can make decisions, take responsibility for his actions, and face difficulties without waiting for others to do everything for him.

In our culture, the family is very close, and the children often depend on their parents for many years. Sometimes a young man of twenty-five still lives with his parents and they cook for him and wash his clothes. This situation is comfortable, but it does not help him to develop his personality. For this reason, I think parents should teach their children to be independent from an early age.

However, self-reliance does not mean that a person should never ask for help. Everyone needs support from friends, teachers, or colleagues. The important thing is to know the difference between the help that makes us stronger and the help that makes us weaker.

In conclusion, self-reliance is a valuable skill for the individual and for the society. A nation of people who can think and act by themselves will be more productive and more confident in the future.

prompt: Write an essay about self-reliance.
text:
The self-reliance is the ability of the person to take care of himself and to make decisions without the constant help of the others. I think this quality is very important in the modern world, where the people often have to move to the other countries, change the jobs and face the difficult situations alone.

When I was a student, I had to live in the other city, far from my parents. At the beginning it was very hard. I did not know how to cook properly, how to manage the money and how to solve the problems with the landlord. But gradually I learned the things which I did not know before, and now I feel more confident in the life. The self-reliance gave me the freedom, but also the responsibility.

On the other hand, the self-reliance should not become the isolation. Sometimes the people refuse the help from the friends or the family because they want to prove something. In my opinion, it is the wrong kind of pride. The real strength is to know when you need the help and to ask for it without the shame.

To sum up, the self-reliance is the important skill, and the parents and the schools should teach it to the children from the early age. But the good self-reliance also includes the understanding that nobody can live completely alone.

prompt: Write an essay about self-reliance.
text:
Self-reliance is often praised as a core virtue, the ability to make decisions, handle challenges, and take responsibility without constantly depending on other people. People who build this skill usually end up more confident and adaptable, which matters a lot now that careers change all the time and lots of people move far from home.

It usually starts with basic practical stuff. Cooking a meal, managing a budget, or sorting out a fight with your landlord builds a kind of confidence you can't get from lectures. Every small win kinda reinforces the idea that u can handle whatever comes.

Still, self-reliance can easily turn into isolation. Some people refuse help even when it would obviously help them, and they confuse needing support with being weak. That can lead to burnout, dumb avoidable mistakes, or relationships that feel one-sided. Asking for support is actually a sign of good judgment about your limits.

The healthiest version is a mix. Be capable of acting on your own, but accept that nobody really succeeds alone. You can grow strong without losing the people who keep you going.

prompt: Write an essay about self-reliance.
text:

Then I got the flu and couldn't get out of bed for three days. Nobody knew. I ate crackers and felt sorry for myself. I think that's when I realized my independence was partly a kind of fear. I didn't want to be a burden, so I just didn't tell anyone things.

text:

If school goes later, theres supervision and food and maybe help with homework. For parents who work all day that would be a huge help. My little brother would love to do robotics after school instead of just waiting for mom.

But honestly i dont think a longer day is always better. By the time i get home from school i am already exhausted. So maybe the answer is not longer days for everybody but more choice. Let kids pick the clubs or tutoring they want and make it optional. Thats what i think anyway.

prompt: Write an essay about an extended school day.
text:
Many education systems are now considering an extended school day, in which students stay at school until late afternoon. Supporters of this idea believe that longer hours will give students more time to study and to practice the skills they need. Also, the extra time can be used for sports, arts, and clubs, which are very important for the development of the children.

Another advantage is that working parents will have a safe place for their children until they finish their work. Many children in the cities are alone at home in the afternoon, and this can be dangerous for them. In the school, they can be supervised by teachers and they can eat a healthy meal.

However, I think there are some serious disadvantages. Children need time to rest and to play with their families. If the school day becomes very long, the students will be tired and they will not concentrate well in the class. In addition, the quality of teaching may decline because the teachers will also be exhausted.

In my opinion, the extended school day can be useful, but it should be flexible. Students should have the choice to participate in the extra activities, and the school should not force them to stay for many hours every day. The balance between the study and the rest is the key to success.

prompt: Write an essay about an extended school day.
text:
The extended school day is the topic of many discussions in our country now. The idea is that children will stay at the school until the evening, and they will have the lessons, the homework help, the sport and the creative activities in the same place. Supporters think it is good for the education, because the children will have more time for the study and less time for the computer games.

From my point of view, the main advantage is for the working parents. Many mothers and fathers cannot leave the work early, and the children are often alone at home after the school. The extended day gives them the safe place and the supervision. Also, the children from the poor families can get the hot meal at the school, which is very important.

But I have some doubts about the effectiveness. The children are already tired after the regular lessons, and if they stay longer, they will be less attentive. The teachers also will be tired, and the quality of the teaching can decrease. The extra hours should be the time for the interesting activities, not just the sitting in the classroom.

So, I think the extended day is the reasonable idea, but it must be optional and well organized. The children should have the free time for the rest, the family and the hobbies.

prompt: Write an essay about an extended school day.
text:
Some districts are thinking about extending the school day into the late afternoon. The argument is that extra hours could deepen learning and give more kids access to tutoring, sports, arts, and clubs they don't get after the final bell now. For families with tight schedules, a supervised place with a meal could be a real help.

But people worry about tiredness. Teenagers already spend a long day in class, and adding hours might make them less focused, not more. Teachers could burn out too, which would hurt the quality of teaching. Just making the day longer doesn't mean the time gets used well.

A better idea might be making the extra hours optional. Schools could offer activities kids actually want, and nobody should be pressured to stay if they need rest. The real test should be what happens during the extra time, not how long kids are stuck on campus.

So an extended day should help students' wellbeing as well as their grades. Done well it could be great. Done carelessly it turns school into something nobody can escape from.

prompt: Write an essay about an extended school day.
text:
When I was in eighth grade our school tried a 'late bus' program for about a semester. It was supposed to be homework help and basketball. In practice it was an hour of sitting in the cafeteria next to kids who were also just waiting for their parents to finish work. The basketball was great though. I'm still decent at free throws, which I attribute entirely to those afternoons.

prompt: Write an essay about imagination.
text:
Imagination lets the mind picture stuff that isn't there yet, like a fictional world, a scientific hypothesis, or a better design for an everyday object. It's usually linked to childhood play, but it matters just as much in adult life, shaping how people plan, invent, and understand each other.

Scientists often start by imagining possibilities the evidence can't confirm yet. Engineers picture how a structure will handle stress before they build it. Even in math a solution is often glimpsed before it's proven. In each case imagination is kind of a bridge between what we know and what might be true.

It also helps with empathy. When you picture what someone else is going through, you can get perspectives that are different from yours. Books have been doing this for ages, letting readers live lives really far from their own.

But imagination gets ignored when school rewards memorizing and the right answer above everything else. Encouraging kids to ask open questions and make up solutions might be one of the most important things a school can do, since future problems will need people who can think past what's familiar.
